sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Global request limit settings
sections.what: Creates one shared limiter that allows 100 requests per minute per client and returns a standard rate-limit error message.
sections.why: Protects all routes with one rule.
sections.watch_out: The limit is applied to every route, including those used by normal screens, so a limit change affects all users.

summary: Caps each client at 100 requests per minute across the API.
purpose: Protects the server from being flooded by one client.
why: Likely reason: to limit abuse or runaway scripts. Not stated in the code.
how: 1. Counts requests per client address within a one-minute window. 2. Lets requests through until 100 have been used. 3. Refuses further requests with a message and the code RATE_LIMITED. 4. Sends standard rate-limit headers and omits the older style.
inputs: Each incoming request and its client address.
outputs: Either the request continues, or a rate-limit error is returned.
risks: Clients are counted by address, so if the server sits behind a proxy and does not read the real client address, all users may share one limit. The limit applies to every route and is fixed in code, so changing it needs a deploy.
debug: If users see RATE_LIMITED, check which address the server sees for them and remember the window is one minute. The response headers show the remaining quota.
